cases.sentence: Небо и горизонт были одного и того же цвета ___.
cases.explain: «мутной воды» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: It was a warm rainy autumn day. The sky and the horizon were both the color of muddy water. At times a sort of mist descended, and then suddenly heavy slanting rain came down.

cases.sentence: То падал как будто туман, то вдруг припускал косой, ___.

cases.translation: It was a warm rainy autumn day. The sky and the horizon were both the color of muddy water. At times a sort of mist descended, and then suddenly heavy slanting rain came down.

cases.sentence: Он так же, как и его лошадь, косившая голову и поджимавшая уши, морщился от ___ и озабоченно присматривался вперед.
cases.explain: «косого дождя» — after the preposition «от», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: Denísov in a felt cloak and a sheepskin cap from which the rain ran down was riding a thin thoroughbred horse with sunken sides. Like his horse, which turned its head and laid its ears back, he shrank from the driving rain and gazed anxiously before him. His thin face with its short, thick black beard looked angry.

cases.sentence: Рядом с Денисовым, также в бурке и папахе, на сытом, ___ ехал казачий эсаул — сотрудник Денисова.
cases.explain: «крупном донце» — the prepositional is used only after a preposition, for location or topic.
cases.translation: Beside Denísov rode an esaul,116 Denísov’s fellow worker, also in felt cloak and sheepskin cap, and riding a large sleek Don horse.

cases.sentence: Рядом с Денисовым, также в бурке и папахе, на сытом, крупном донце ехал ___ — сотрудник Денисова.

cases.translation: Beside Denísov rode an esaul,116 Denísov’s fellow worker, also in felt cloak and sheepskin cap, and riding a large sleek Don horse.

cases.sentence: Эсаул Ловайский — третий, также в бурке и папахе, был длинный, плоский как доска, белолицый, белокурый человек с узкими, светлыми глазками и спокойно ___ и в лице и в посадке.
cases.explain: «самодовольным выражением» — after the preposition «с», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: Esaul Lováyski the Third was a tall man as straight as an arrow, pale-faced, fair-haired, with narrow light eyes and with calm self-satisfaction in his face and bearing. Though it was impossible to say in what the peculiarity of the horse and rider lay, yet at first glance at the esaul and Denísov one saw that the latter was wet and uncomfortable and was a man mounted on a horse, while looking at the esaul one saw that he was as comfortable and as much at ease as always and that he was not a man who had mounted a horse, but a man who was one with his horse, a being consequently possessed of twofold strength.

cases.sentence: Немного впереди их шел насквозь промокший мужичок проводник, в ___ и белом колпаке.
cases.explain: «сером кафтане» — after the preposition «в», for location or topic.
cases.translation: A little ahead of them walked a peasant guide, wet to the skin and wearing a gray peasant coat and a white knitted cap.

cases.sentence: Немного впереди их шел насквозь промокший мужичок проводник, в сером кафтане и ___.

cases.sentence: Немного сзади, на худой, тонкой, киргизской лошаденке с ___ и гривой и с продранными в кровь губами, ехал молодой офицер в синей, французской шинели.
cases.explain: «огромным хвостом» — after the preposition «с», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: A little behind, on a poor, small, lean Kirghíz mount with an enormous tail and mane and a bleeding mouth, rode a young officer in a blue French overcoat.

cases.sentence: Немного сзади, на худой, тонкой, киргизской лошаденке с огромным хвостом и гривой и с продранными в кровь губами, ехал ___ в синей, французской шинели.
cases.explain: «молодой офицер» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: A little behind, on a poor, small, lean Kirghíz mount with an enormous tail and mane and a bleeding mouth, rode a young officer in a blue French overcoat.

cases.sentence: Рядом с ним ехал гусар, везя за собой на крупе лошади мальчика в французском ___ и синем колпаке.
cases.explain: «оборванном мундире» — after the preposition «в», for location or topic.
cases.translation: Beside him rode an hussar, with a boy in a tattered French uniform and blue cap behind him on the crupper of his horse. The boy held on to the hussar with cold, red hands, and raising his eyebrows gazed about him with surprise. This was the French drummer boy captured that morning.

cases.sentence: Мальчик держался красными от холода руками за гусара, пошевеливал, стараясь согреть их, свои ___, и, подняв брови, удивленно оглядывался вокруг себя.
cases.explain: «босые ноги» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.

The boy held on to the hussar with cold, red hands, and raising his eyebrows gazed about him with surprise. This was the French drummer boy captured that morning.

cases.translation: Beside him rode an hussar, with a boy in a tattered French uniform and blue cap behind him on the crupper of his horse. The boy held on to the hussar with cold, red hands, and raising his eyebrows gazed about him with surprise. This was the French drummer boy captured that morning.

cases.sentence: Сзади по три, по четыре, по узкой, раскиснувшей и изъезженной ___, тянулись гусары, потом казаки, кто в бурке, кто во французской шинели, кто в попоне, накинутой на голову.
cases.explain: «лесной дороге» — after the preposition «по», the dative marks the indirect object or recipient.
cases.translation: Behind them along the narrow, sodden, cut-up forest road came hussars in threes and fours, and then Cossacks: some in felt cloaks, some in French greatcoats, and some with horsecloths over their heads. The horses, being drenched by the rain, all looked black whether chestnut or bay. Their necks, with their wet, close-clinging manes, looked strangely thin. Steam rose from them. Clothes, saddles, reins, were all wet, slippery, and sodden, like the ground and the fallen leaves that strewed the road. The men sat huddled up trying not to stir, so as to warm the water that had trickled to their bodies and not admit the fresh cold water that was leaking in under their seats, their knees, and at the back of their necks. In the midst of the outspread line of Cossacks two wagons, drawn by French horses and by saddled Cossack horses that had been hitched on in front, rumbled over the tree stumps and branches and splashed through the water that lay in the ruts.

cases.sentence: Только не предположительно, чтобы был ___, — сказал эсаул, любивший употреблять неизвестные казакам слова.
cases.explain: «сам подполковник» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “There are two, an officer and a Cossack. But it is not presupposable that it is the lieutenant colonel himself,” said the esaul, who was fond of using words the Cossacks did not know.

cases.sentence: Офицер этот, очень ___, с широким, румяным лицом и быстрыми, веселыми глазами, подскакал к Денисову и подал ему промокший конверт.
cases.explain: «молоденький мальчик» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: The approaching riders having descended a decline were no longer visible, but they reappeared a few minutes later. In front, at a weary gallop and using his leather whip, rode an officer, disheveled and drenched, whose trousers had worked up to above his knees. Behind him, standing in the stirrups, trotted a Cossack. The officer, a very young lad with a broad rosy face and keen merry eyes, galloped up to Denísov and handed him a sodden envelope.

cases.sentence: — Да ты можешь ли остаться до ___?
cases.explain: «завтрашнего дня» — after the preposition «до», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: “Orders?” Denísov repeated thoughtfully. “But can you stay till tomowwow?”

cases.sentence: Сам же Денисов с эсаулом и Петей намеревался подъехать к опушке леса, выходившей к Шамшеву, с тем чтобы взглянуть на то место расположения французов, на которое должно было быть направлено ___.
cases.explain: «завтрашнее нападение» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Well, all wight,” said Denísov. And turning to his men he directed a party to go on to the halting place arranged near the watchman’s hut in the forest, and told the officer on the Kirghíz horse (who performed the duties of an adjutant) to go and find out where Dólokhov was and whether he would come that evening. Denísov himself intended going with the esaul and Pétya to the edge of the forest where it reached out to Shámshevo, to have a look at the part of the French bivouac they were to attack next day.
